subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Anchoring: First Numbers Stick
description: A 60-second lesson on Anchoring: First Numbers Stick.

hook.text: Spin a wheel labeled 10 or 65. Then guess Africa's UN membership. Your answer drifts toward the wheel.

buildup.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed that random numbers influence unrelated estimates. The anchor pulls you.

discovery.text: Anchoring: the first number you hear sets a reference point. All later estimates adjust from it.

twist.text: Even experts anchor. Judges given random dice rolls before sentencing gave different sentence lengths.

climax.text: Whoever sets the first number controls the negotiation. The anchor defines the playing field.

punchline.text: The first number wins half the argument.

quiz.question: What does the anchoring heuristic show?
options: Initial numbers influence later estimates even if irrelevant

details.summary: Anchoring shows that the first number encountered in a judgment context disproportionately influences subsequent estimates. Even random numbers shift people's answers toward the anchor, demonstrating that initial information creates a gravitational pull on all later thinking.
details.whyItMatters: Anchoring affects salary negotiations, real estate pricing, damage awards, and budget planning. Understanding this heuristic explains why first offers matter so much and why seemingly irrelevant numbers can skew professional judgment.
takeaways: First numbers encountered pull subsequent estimates toward them
Even obviously irrelevant anchors affect expert estimates
The anchor sets a starting point from which adjustment is typically insufficient

faq.question: Can anchoring bias be eliminated by awareness alone?
faq.answer: No. Studies show that knowing about anchoring reduces but does not eliminate its effect. Even trained professionals who are warned about anchoring still exhibit significant anchor-consistent bias. Deliberate counter-anchoring strategies are needed.

faq.question: How can you use anchoring strategically in negotiations?
faq.answer: Make the first offer to set the anchor in your favor. Ensure your opening number is ambitious but defensible. Research shows that final agreements are more strongly correlated with the opening offer than with any subsequent counter-offers.
